objective: Publish one authoritative, machine-readable scenario capability matrix that names, for every registered scenario identity, its semantic actions, required adapters, evidence status, verifier, recovery policy and owner, and make a registry entry without a matrix row fail a deterministic validation command.
decision_supported: Whether a contributor can tell from one committed artifact what each scenario can do, which boundary owns it, and how strong its evidence is, instead of inferring support from a fixture passing.
acceptance: the matrix carries one row for every registered scenario identity and for every task family that is planned, blocked or not yet registered, so a missing family is visible rather than silent
every row declares semantic actions, required adapters, evidence status, verifier, recovery policy, environment status and owner
the matrix validator fails a registry entry that has no matrix row, and fails a matrix row that names an unregistered identity, so the two artifacts cannot drift
matrix status distinguishes software, scripted fixture, Gazebo and physical evidence, and no row infers a stronger status than its manifest declares
a row may not name joint trajectories, controller goals, torque or velocity limits, CAN frames or emergency-stop authority
the matrix declares ownership for scenario rules, adapter implementation, evidence and release decision by reference to the ADR-0006 ownership table
the generated markdown table is reproducible from the JSON and is byte-identical across runs
the validator imports no ROS, Gazebo, MoveIt or hardware module and writes nothing
an absent, unreadable or unparseable matrix is INCOMPLETE rather than a silent pass
evidence: pytest transcript for tests/unit/test_scenario_capabilities.py with the passed count
check_scenario_capabilities.py stdout showing the matrix row count, the registered identities covered and exit code 0
check_scenario_capabilities.py --check-generated output proving the committed markdown table matches the JSON
the failure transcript showing a registry entry without a row exits 1 with a stable MATRIX_* code
ruff check and ruff format output
make scenario-check, make contract and make context-check output
stop_conditions: the change would require editing docs/architecture/scenario-contract-v1.json or the frozen public schema, which is a reviewed contract amendment and belongs to a separate Issue
the change would require registering a new scenario identity, which belongs to Issue #301 or Issue #306
the change would require extending the shared ActionType vocabulary, which belongs to Issue #306
the change would require a new runtime dependency or any ROS, Gazebo or hardware import
a frozen scenario fixture would have to be renamed, re-seeded or re-hashed
data_classification: public repository source, documentation and test fixtures; no secrets, personal data, credentials or physical measurement data
model_policy: AI may write the matrix, the validator, the generated table and the tests; a named human Owner accepts the ownership map and any row that claims an evidence status
risks_and_fallbacks: the matrix could be read as a claim that a scenario runs; fallback is that every row carries an explicit environment status and the validator refuses a status stronger than the manifest evidence_status
the matrix could drift from the registry; fallback is that the validator fails a registry identity without a row and a row without a registration, in both directions
the generated markdown could silently diverge from the JSON; fallback is that --check-generated regenerates and compares byte-for-byte
a planned family row could be mistaken for a delivered capability; fallback is that planned and blocked statuses are explicit vocabulary values and never release eligible
rollback is a revert of this commit; the matrix is additive documentation plus a read-only validator and no runtime path imports it
